newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: CRICKET-VICTORIA HANG ON FOR DRAW AGAINST QUEENSLAND.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-VICTORIA HANG ON FOR DRAW AGAINST QUEENSLAND.

text.p: Victoria captain Tony Dodemaide and tail-ender David Saker led a rearguard action on Saturday to enable their side to hang on for a draw on the final day of their Sheffield Shield match against Queensland.
Set an unlikely target of 394 to win, Victoria appeared headed for defeat after falling to 189 for eight with 24 overs of play remaining at the Melbourne Cricket Ground.
Dodemaide and Saker however defied the Queensland bowlers to take the home side to 213 for eight before play was stopped.
Dodemaide finished unbeaten on 14 and Saker was 11 not out. Number three batsman Brendan Ricci top-scored for Victoria with 43 while opener Graeme Vimpani made 32.

Queensland captain Stuart Law earlier declared his side's second innings closed on its overnight score of 355 for four and his bowlers looked set to press home the advantage as Victoria fell to 163 for six at tea.
Victoria are now in fifth place in the six-team Shield competition and have virtually no chance of qualifying for next month's final, while Queensland are in equal second place with New South Wales.
